content.text:
Changing the props of `TelegramLinkWidget` (`app/portal/components/TelegramLinkWidget.tsx`) affects two pages directly. Its props are `role?: "reseller" | "supplier"` (default `"reseller"`) and `className?: string` (default `""`).

**Pages affected**
- **`/portal/reseller`**: `app/portal/reseller/page.tsx:741` renders `<TelegramLinkWidget role="reseller" />`.
- **`/portal/supplier`**: `app/portal/supplier/page.tsx:715` renders `<TelegramLinkWidget role="supplier" />`.

Both pages pass only `role`. Neither passes `className`, so changes to `className` alone won't break either call site. If you rename or remove `role`, change its allowed values, or make a new prop required, both pages will need updating.

**Also affected**
- `test/portal-telegram-widget.test.ts` creates the widget with `{ role: "reseller" }` and `{ role: "supplier" }` (lines 14 and 20). Its other two tests, at lines 24 and 33, check that the two pages embed the widget.

I found no other imports or usages outside `node_modules`. The widget calls three API routes: `/api/v2/auth/telegram/status`, `/link-token` and `/unlink`. A change that touches those calls would affect the same two pages, but I didn't read the widget past line 45, so I can't say how `role` is used inside it.
